properties.title: 🎃🐾 LI-DOG Howl-O-Ween Costume Contest & Pawty! 🐾🎃
properties.description:
**Calling all spooky pups, silly mutts, and dressed-up doggos—it’s time to unleash the fun!** LI-DOG is taking over The Pine Grove Inn for an afternoon packed with creative costumes, festive activities, and plenty of reasons for dogs and their people to celebrate together.

**Costume Contest**

Turn PGI’s back lawn into your pup’s personal runway! Bring out the capes, crowns, clever characters, and coordinated ensembles for a costume contest where originality gets its moment in the spotlight. There are two categories in our contest:

1. **Best Standalone Pet:** Whether your pup is a werewolf, taco, fairy or hot dog, we can’t wait to see your creativity!
2. **Best Dog & Human Team:** Pair up for a themed costume that shows off your imagination: a pup pilot and his flight crew? Cruella deVil and her Dalmatians? Old McDonald and his farm animals?

**We're thrilled to thank Pet Wants Great South Bay for generously sponsoring our costume contest prizes!** Thanks to their support, the top three costume contest winners in each category will share **$300 in prizes!** Pet Wants offers all-natural food, chews, treats and supplements for dogs and cats. Be sure to stop by their booth and check out their products.

**Our Costume Contest kicks off at 1 p.m., so make sure you're at the Pawty by then!**

**More Pawty Highlights**

1. 🍬 **Tasty Treats for Pups and their People:** Delicious food and HowloWeen-themed drinks for purchase from the Pine Grove Inn's extensive menu from salads and sandwiches to pasta and dessert.
2. **Free Doggie Cake** for all the good boys and girls in attendance. Thank you to Who Lets Your Dog Out dog care services for generously donating a pup cake for our canine guests!
3. 📸 **Picture-Perfect Moments:** Pose against a playful Halloween backdrop filled with pumpkins, spooky scenery, and seasonal flair.
4. 🎨 **Make-and-Take Fun:** Create a paw-print painting with your dog or decorate a spooky Halloween-themed cutout to bring home as a festive memento.

🎃🐾 **Special Guests:** Visit with our fabulous VIPs (Very Important Pet vendors) sharing dog-friendly goodies and gear and valuable resources and services for you and your four-legged family members.

1. **All-Island K9 Services** will do a short training demonstration and be available to discuss your training needs.
2. **Wyldfire Photography** will be on hand ready to snap picture-perfect shots of you and your pup dressed for the pawty.
3. **Bark and Bead** will be there with their festive handmade beaded collars and matching bracelets.
4. **Community Pet Supplies** will have treats, toys, and information on their upcoming Photos with Santa event.
5. **Dog Days Pet Care** will be there with information about their dog walking & pet sitting services and tasty treats for the pups.
6. **Farmina Foods** will tell you about their healthy pet meals and offer your pup a tasty morsel. Farmina is also donating goody bags for our first 30 to 40 guests!
7. **NY Safe Haven Animal Rescue** will bring their adorable adoptable pups to the event. Who knows you may find your dog's new best friend!
8. **Pet Wants Great South Bay**. Discover fresh, healthy pet food and all-natural treats made for your furry family.
9. **URvetCare** will talk about the services they offer at their new 24/7 emergency and walk-in veterinary hospital on Long Island.
10. W**ho Lets Your Dog Out** dog walking and dog care services will have toys, accessories and handmade pottery at their booth. They'll also set up a backyard-scale agility course so your pup can try out their jumping and weaving skills.

**🎵 Music—spooky, fun and upbeat--provided by our DJ Mike Kaplow and his trusty sidekick Ms. Maroney.** Enjoy a playlist filled with tunes that everyone—humans and pups alike—can enjoy.

**Grand Raffle Prize! A Chance to Fly with Your Dog on RetrievAir!** LI-DOG is excited to announce that RetrievAir--the airline where dogs ride in the cabin with their families that now flies from Long Island's MacArthur Airport--has donated a $1,000 flight voucher (valid thru Oct. 2027) as our Grand Raffle Prize! Thank you, RetrievAir, for your extremely generous donation. Make sure to enter our Howl-o-Ween raffle for a chance to win this fantastic prize! Must be present to win.

**🧺 The fun doesn't stop there. Our wonderful sponsors have generously donated GREAT raffle baskets, too!** From goodies for our dogs to hand-crafted gifts for you, be sure to purchase raffle tickets for a chance to win one of the terrific raffle baskets donated by our sponsors—All Island K9 Services, Behr's Boutique, Brutus Bone Broth, Community Pet Supplies, The Fish Store Market & Restaurant, Health Extension Pet Products, Laura Pea Photography, Alan Meschkow, Gail Meschkow, Momo's Too Sports Bar, Pindar Vineyards, Stew Leonard's, Stop & Shop and Who Lets Your Dog Out among others.

**A lovely setting!** Imagine a big lawn with a lazy river flowing by, a pretty gazebo in the corner, and tables with umbrellas on a brick patio with an outdoor bar serving Howl-o-Ween themed drinks nearby. That’s the Pine Grove Inn!

👥 **Open to all dog lovers—costumes encouraged but not required.**
**Our Howl-o-Ween Pawty is an important fundraiser for LI-DOG,** which works to get more access to public parks and beaches on Long Island for dog owners and their pups!

So, grab your dog-loving friends and family and join us on November1st for what should be a lot of fun AND a great way to support LI-DOG’s work!

**Discounted advance tickets for $15 per person are now available for purchase from the [LI-DOG website](https://lidog.org/events/li-dog-howl-o-ween-costume-contest-pawty-2026/).** On the day of the event, tickets will be $20 per person. Dogs and children 12 and under are FREE.

**Discounted advance ticket sales end at NOON on SATURDAY.**

**To RSVP, go to:**
Here on Meetup
LI-DOG on Facebook
[Howl-O-Ween Pawty at The Pine Grove Inn](https://www.facebook.com/events/2152787198671199/?acontext=%7B%22event_action_history%22%3A%5B%7B%22mechanism%22%3A%22attachment%22%2C%22surface%22%3A%22newsfeed%22%7D%5D%2C%22ref_notif_type%22%3Anull%7D)
or email [events@lidog.org](mailto:events@lidog.org)

🙋 **Help Make the Pawty a Success!**
**We need volunteers to help make our pawty happen!** Email us at [events@lidog.org](http://events@lidog.org/) with Howl-o-ween Pawty Volunteer in the subject line if you’d to help decorate the venue, set up our raffles, or participate in other ways.

**Sponsorship Opportunities Available!**
**Our Howl-o-Ween fundraiser offers several ways for sponsors to connect with engaged, enthusiastic dog owners** by showcasing their products and services from LI-DOG’s website and social media acknowledgements to shout-outs at the event itself.

**To get details,** check out LI-DOG’s [Sponsorship Opportunities](https://lidog.org/sponsorship-opportunities/) page and click on the Howl-o-Ween 2026 Sponsor Opportunities flyer.

**🐾 Important Reminder for Pet Owners**

1. Please be aware dogs must remain leashed on non-retractable leads at all times\*\*.\*\*
2. Please walk your dog before entering the venue.
3. Only service dogs are permitted inside the restaurant.

☁️ **In the event of inclement weather, please check our website,** Facebook, or Meetup the morning of the event. If there is no announcement the Pawty is ON!

**We look forward to seeing you and your pups at LI-DOG’s Howl-o-Ween Pawty & Fundraiser on Sunday, Nov. 1st!**

properties.title: Open Source System Administration Study Group
properties.description:
This group will learn about system administration topics with hands-on collaborative learning on a homelab setup of four Dell servers. A description of this session's plan in down below.
We’ll deploy components like LDAP(authentication), Ansible (Infrastructure as Code), NextCloud (file storage), OpenStack (Cloud computing), OpenTofu (IaC Terraform fork), containerization and other open source software. We also intend to explore clustering, certainly high-availability and possibly compute clustering.

We've setup the hardware, installed the OS, and established procedures and documentation standards. Now we're starting to work in small groups or individually on projects. An under-construction list of project ideas is at https://wiki.hackmanhattan.com/Project_Ideas.

We have room for a few new people. Sign up to this event, come and do the exercise, and you're in.

Join the Hack Manhattan Discord and say hello. DM me there with your email address so I can sign you up for a wiki account.

Please bring a laptop if you can. We'll have a limited number of machines available you can use.

properties.title: Prototyping in Public: Where Art and Science Get Tested on the Gallery Floor
properties.description:
What if a museum ran like a lab, with the experiment still in progress?

**[Ann Neumann](https://www.museumnext.com/speakers/ann-neumann/)** is Director of Galleries and Exhibitions at the **[MIT Museum](https://mitmuseum.mit.edu/)**. Her question for the evening: can a museum serve as infrastructure for public experimentation, **a place where visitors take part in the work** rather than just walk through it?

If you build products, run pilots, or spend your days deciding what's ready to put in front of real people, **this is a look at how one of the best-known science museums handles prototyping in public.**

In collaboration with the **[National Arts Club](https://www.nacnyc.org/)** and its **[Art and Technology Committee](https://www.nacnyc.org/arts-and-programs/committees)**, Ann will walk through the interactive projects she's shepherded at the MIT Museum. **Each one works as a prototype for engaging the public with technologies** like CRISPR, machine learning, and sensory neuroscience.

Reserve your spot and arrive early. Space is limited.

Founded in 1898, the **[National Arts Club](https://www.nacnyc.org/)** is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit with a mission to stimulate, foster, and promote public interest in the arts and to educate the American people in the fine arts.

Annually, the Club offers more than 150 free programs—both in-person and virtually—to the public, including exhibitions, theatrical and musical performances, lectures, and readings, attracting an audience of over 30,000 in-person visitors and thousands more online.

A limited number of founders will have the opportunity to pitch their startup or business **to a panel of investors and experts.**

4-6 selected founders will pitch their startup, followed by a short Q&A where participants can ask questions and share feedback.

Apply by filling out the [Pitch Application Form](https://forms.gle/CuscVQibyXBbi1Fv7) and sending us your pitch deck.

**Requirements for attendees:**

- Dress code: smart casual. Bring good energy.

**🎟 Join our event and secure your ticket today!**

**About us:**

[Startup Valley](https://startupvalley.club/) is a global event organizer hosting pitch nights in 25 cities since 2023. Since then, **we have hosted 850 events for 40,000 attendees**. Over these years, we connected countless outstanding early-stage startups to serious investors, and we are not planning to stop. We maintain strategic partnerships with VC funds in the US, Europe, and Asia to support our community.

**See every upcoming event in New York, with dates and venues:** [New York startup events](https://startupvalley.club/cities/new-york)

Do you have a **question, a partnership proposal, or want to clarify something**? Reach us at hello@startupvalley.club

**Agenda**

- 18:00–18:30 — **Registration**: Guests register, receive badges, and event programs. This is an opportunity for casual networking, making first connections, and preparing for the event.
- 18:30–19:00 — **Event Kickoff & Interactive Networking**: Official welcome from the organizers with a brief overview of the event goals and schedule. Interactive networking session to connect with key contacts.
- 19:00–19:50 — **Startup Pitch Session**: Startups present their projects to investors and experts. Each team has 5 minutes to pitch, covering the project’s core idea, business model, and target market.
- 19:50–21:00 — **Chill & Networking**: Participants enjoy casual conversations with investors, discuss collaboration opportunities, and exchange ideas over refreshments.

**FAQ**

**Can I pitch?**
Yes! To pitch, please purchase a Pitch Ticket and fill out the Pitch Application Form. We will contact you to discuss and approve your pitch. The pitch duration is 5 minutes. You will also have some time to answer questions from the audience.

**How does the pitch go?**
Selected founders present on stage to the audience and the investors in the room. You get 5 minutes to pitch your idea, business model, target market, and investment ask, followed by a short Q&A. The best startups are featured across our social media channels and in the investor newsletter.

**Who will I meet?**
Founders, angel investors, VC partners, venture scouts, AI experts, engineers, operators, marketing and sales experts, and international entrepreneurs from across Europe, Asia, and the US.

**Do investors get free tickets?**
Yes! Email hello@startupvalley.club or apply via Luma (the link is in the event description), and we will issue a complimentary ticket for you and your team.

**Can I request a refund?**
Yes. Refunds are available if requested at least 1 day before the event start time. Please submit the refund request on the platform where you purchased your ticket, or email us at hello@startupvalley.club

properties.title: Designing for a Feeling: MDA, Immersive Experiences & Emerging Technology
properties.description:
What do you want your audience to feel—and how do you design an experience that gets them there?

Join Columbia DSL on Monday, November 9, for an evening with **Nick Fortugno** exploring MDA (Mechanics, Dynamics, and Aesthetics) as a framework for creating compelling immersive experiences.

In MDA, aesthetics refers to the emotional experience of participating: wonder, tension, discovery, connection, belonging. We’ll explore how those feelings emerge through the rules you create, the choices you offer, and the interactions that unfold between participants.

Together, we’ll consider:

* **Mechanics:** What can participants do? What rules and systems shape their choices?
* **Dynamics:** What happens as people interact with those systems and one another?
* **Aesthetics:** What does the experience make people feel?

Whether you’re working with AI, interactive storytelling, games, or live performance, MDA offers a practical way to connect creative intention with audience experience.

Come explore how starting with a feeling can shape what you build.

## About Nick Fortugno

**Nick Fortugno** is a game designer, interactive storyteller, and educator. He is Director of Digital Game Development and a Distinguished Lecturer at The City College of New York, part of CUNY, and co-founder of Playmatics. With more than two decades of experience, his work spans games, immersive experiences, and emerging technology. His credits include lead designer of *Diner Dash* and lead interactive narrative designer on *Frankenstein AI*, presented at Sundance’s New Frontier. **You've been running the idea past ChatGPT. ChatGPT has never once told you it wouldn't work. Tonight you get a room that will.**

Five founders, five minutes each, on a Fifth Avenue rooftop in Manhattan. Wednesday.

**Three reasons people come back**

* You get a table, not a lap of the room. You pick a topic the room voted on and stay there for the hour, instead of wandering with a drink looking for a gap in somebody else's conversation.
* You get a stage short enough to be honest. Five minutes each, no slides read out loud, then the room asks questions. The questions are the good part.
* You get the hour after. The stage ends, nobody's performing any more, and the floor stays open. That's the hour people actually remember.

**Your ticket is also a login**
Most events end when you walk out. This one hands you a link: your profile, who else is coming before you get there, a group chat for this specific Wednesday, and a recap afterwards of who you actually met.

Then you land in the New York space and stay there. That's where the second conversation happens, the one you meant to have before the room got loud.

Free with your ticket, on the web or in Telegram: [ascentvalley.com/community](https://ascentvalley.com/community "https://ascentvalley.com/community")

**Is this your room?**
Yes, if you're building something, anywhere from the first line of code to Series A. Or you run a function at a company that's scaling, write the code, do the hiring, or you're still deciding whether to start.

Probably not, if what you're picturing is a room full of investors. How that actually works is further down, and it's better than the picture.

**Want the stage?**
Apply at ascentvalley.com/pitch. Five founders an evening, and we answer everybody, including the people we don't pick. Applying is free, but you do need a ticket, because we check the order number.

Never pitched before? Five minutes is short enough that it's over before the nerves have finished arriving.

**What we don't promise, and what we do instead**
We don't promise an investor will be in the room on any given Wednesday. Angels and people who work at funds come, some Wednesdays several of them, and we won't tell you in advance who's coming, because we don't know.

We don't run a judging panel, hand out a prize, or keep a leaderboard.

Here's what doesn't depend on who walks in that night. Your application to the stage becomes your profile in our startup directory, and a person reads it, not a scoring script.

Once you're verified, that profile sits in front of the funds and angels in our network, and they ask for the introduction themselves when your company matches what they're actually looking for.

You choose whether you're in the weekly digest and you can leave it any time. We never sell your details, we don't take equity, we don't take a cut of your round, and we don't give investment advice.

Which means the room on Wednesday isn't the whole opportunity. It's the part you can see: [ascentvalley.com/pitch](https://ascentvalley.com/pitch "https://ascentvalley.com/pitch")

**Why it's worth a Wednesday**
Watching somebody explain their company in five minutes teaches you more about explaining yours than another evening alone with the deck.

You'll hear the question you've been quietly avoiding get asked out loud to somebody else, and you get to watch how they handle it.

That skill travels. It works on a first date, in a performance review, and at the dinner where somebody asks what you do and you've got twenty seconds before their eyes move on.

So bring the friend who keeps saying they have an idea. Five minutes on that stage is the shortest distance between having an idea and finding out what a room full of strangers thinks of it.

Get ready to stuff your faces with knowledge with this month's GolangNYC meetup and learn about building on top of the Go compiler's Static Single Assignment (SSA) and a technical deep dive of [gohawk](https://gohawk.dev/) with James Ko.

**Talk Synopsis:**
As AI-generated code becomes more common, static analysis tooling is becoming more and more invaluable as a way to catch programming errors before they happen at runtime. This talk will provide an overview of Gohawk, a static analyzer that flags resource leaks and concurrency issues in Go code. It will include a technical deep dive that explains how it builds on Go SSA to perform interprocedural analysis.
